docs.D00_original_thesis.md:
Title: Original owner thesis — consumer habit, store returns and temporary operating disappointment
Source: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/10/07150943/2018-Annual-Report-Letter-Only.pdf
Date: 2019-03-25

This is an archival copy of the 2018 annual manager letter, published in March 2019. The hosting path does not change the historical information date. It explains an investment established in 2018, not the decision at the current cutoff.

The manager calls Starbucks the dominant global specialty-coffee brand, with roughly 30,000 owned/licensed stores and $35 billion annual system sales. It emphasizes a loyal customer base with a frequent consumption habit and trade-up potential, protected by advantages over low-cost and boutique competitors.

The letter describes Starbucks as a rare large business with a long runway to reinvest at high returns. It estimates new-store pretax returns of 55% in the US and 75% in China. These are the manager's store-level estimates, not consolidated GAAP ROIC.

The manager expects high-single-digit revenue growth from underpenetrated markets, especially China, and same-store product innovation. Chinese per-capita coffee consumption is described as less than 1% of US levels; that indicates possible runway but does not guarantee Starbucks captures it profitably.

The entry valuation argument is explicit: shares had been roughly flat over three years while earnings rose 50%, allowing purchase at a 25% discount to the company's historical average of 26 times forward earnings. The letter reports an average $51.30 purchase price for the PSH investment.

The perceived discount reflected slowing US comparable sales, questions about long-term targets and management turnover. The thesis was operating improvement and continued franchise growth, not a hostile proxy contest.

By the letter date, the manager cites US same-store sales growth of 4% in each of the previous two quarters, following four quarters of 1%-2%. Initiatives include Nitro, marketing to less frequent customers, rewards changes, delivery and overhead simplification.

The letter also welcomes a $20 billion repurchase program expected to reduce shares roughly 20% over 2018-2020. It says prospective returns remained compelling despite appreciation already achieved. That was the historical owner's judgment in March 2019, not a statement of the appropriate action in January 2020.

The present evaluation must distinguish a continuing attractive business from a continuing attractive price. Successful execution can validate the original operating thesis while simultaneously reducing the remaining valuation discount.
docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Global coffee franchise, owned stores and licensed distribution
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/829224/000082922419000047/sbux-9292019xexhibit991.htm; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/10/07150943/2018-Annual-Report-Letter-Only.pdf
Date: 2019-10-30

Starbucks combines a global coffee brand, a company-operated store network, licensed stores and packaged/channel distribution. Its proposition includes coffee quality, convenience, customization, a familiar store experience and a rewards/digital relationship with frequent customers.

The company ended FY2019 with 31,256 stores, up 7% year over year. Store expansion and comparable-store activity are separate growth drivers: a mature location's traffic/check trends cannot be inferred from consolidated growth alone.

In the fourth quarter, company-operated store revenue was $5,480.1 million and licensed-store revenue $734.7 million. These business models have different recorded revenue and capital requirements. Licensed sales are not the full retail sales of the franchisee's store.

The global coffee alliance with Nestlé changes the channel-business mix and cash-flow interpretation. Transactional cash receipts and subsequent recognition should not be valued as if the same upfront proceeds recur every year.

US active rewards membership reached 17.6 million in Q4, up 15%. Rewards, mobile ordering, beverage innovation and convenience can reinforce customer frequency and retention. Their economic value depends on incremental profitable transactions rather than signups alone.

China remains a key growth market, with Q4 comparable sales up 5% and net store growth of 17% year over year. It also creates country, competition and execution exposure. Low historical per-capita consumption is an opportunity indicator, not a guaranteed market-share forecast.

CEO Kevin Johnson's team has focused on streamlining operations and prioritizing core growth. The company's October outlook reaffirms its long-term operating growth model. There is no pre-cutoff announcement in these documents of a fundamental abandonment of the coffee franchise or China growth strategy.

The moat thesis rests on habitual demand, brand, convenient locations and a broad consumer relationship. It is not immunity from wage inflation, competition, changes in consumer tastes or poorly chosen new sites.

The investor's question is therefore two-part: whether franchise quality remains intact, and whether the prospective per-share growth and cash distributions justify the current valuation. A well-run, growing company can offer a lower future return after a strong rerating without becoming an impaired business.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Three fiscal years, cash flow and capital returns
Source: compiled from: https://s203.q4cdn.com/326826266/files/doc_financials/2017/q4/Q4-17-Earnings-Release-Final.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/829224/000082922419000047/sbux-9292019xexhibit991.htm
Date: 2019-10-30

Dollars are millions except EPS. Fiscal years end around September; 2017 and 2019 have 52 weeks. GAAP and adjusted earnings differ materially because of transactions and restructuring.

| Metric | FY2017 | FY2018 | FY2019 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 22,386.8 | 24,719.5 | 26,508.6 |
| GAAP operating income | 4,134.7 | 3,883.3 | 4,077.9 |
| GAAP operating margin, calculated | 18.5% | 15.7% | 15.4% |
| GAAP diluted EPS | 1.97 | 3.24 | 2.92 |
| CFO | 4,251.8 | 11,937.8 | 5,047.0 |
| Capital additions | 1,519.4 | 1,976.4 | 1,806.6 |
| CFO less capital additions, calculated | 2,732.4 | 9,961.4 | 3,240.4 |

FY2018 cash flow includes a major transaction-related receipt associated with the Nestlé alliance. It is not a normalized recurring FCF base. Similarly, the FY2018 East China acquisition-related gain affects GAAP EPS comparability.

Non-GAAP EPS was $2.42 in FY2018 and $2.83 in FY2019, approximately 17% growth. That underlying improvement contrasts with the decline in GAAP EPS, demonstrating why neither single series should be used without its reconciliation.

FY2019 repurchases were $10,222.3 million versus $7,133.5 million in FY2018. The diluted weighted-average share count fell from 1,394.6 million to 1,233.2 million, while ending outstanding shares fell from 1,309.1 million to 1,184.6 million.

Cash at FY2019 end was $2,686.6 million. Long-term debt was $11,167.0 million. The retrieved balance sheet has no separate current long-term-debt amount for 2019; a full debt/lease reconciliation is not supplied. Simple long-term debt less cash is $8,480.4 million before other adjustments.

The capital-return program is substantial relative to current recurring cash generation and uses transaction cash/financing as well as current earnings. Buybacks reduce the EPS denominator but do not automatically create value at every purchase price.

A historical consolidated ROIC series was not recovered. Store-level pretax-return estimates in the original owner letter are not a substitute. The key forward question is normalized operating growth and sustainable cash returns, not repeating the unusually large FY2018 cash inflow.
docs.D03_latest_results.md:
Title: Q4 results show improved traffic, rewards engagement and China growth
Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/829224/000082922419000047/sbux-9292019xexhibit991.htm
Date: 2019-10-30

Starbucks' latest available earnings release is the October 30 report for the fiscal quarter/year ended September 29. The January 28, 2020 release is outside the cutoff even though its fiscal quarter ended in December.

Q4 comparable-store sales grew 5% globally, led by 6% in the US and 5% in China. Global net store growth was 7%, including 17% net growth in China. The release presents both existing-store performance and continued system expansion.

Quarterly GAAP EPS was $0.67. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.70, up 13% year over year. The distinction reflects items excluded in the company's reconciliation and should not be blurred when computing a forward multiple.

US active rewards membership increased 15% to 17.6 million. The company has been using beverage innovation, digital convenience and loyalty engagement to improve operating performance. Membership growth is supportive evidence, while transaction and profitability data remain necessary to establish incremental economics.

FY2019 revenue reached $26.509 billion. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.83 compared with $2.42 in FY2018, despite lower GAAP EPS caused by the prior-year transaction effects.

For FY2020, management guides consolidated GAAP revenue growth of 6%-8% and operating income growth of 8%-10%. Non-GAAP EPS guidance is $3.00-$3.05; GAAP EPS guidance is $2.84-$2.89.

Capital expenditures are projected at approximately $1.8 billion. This is required investment in a growing owned-store network as well as the broader platform, not a negligible franchise-only cost structure.

The forward adjusted EPS midpoint of $3.025 implies growth of roughly 6.9% from $2.83. That is below the historical adjusted EPS growth just delivered and should be distinguished from the longer-term model or a bull-case acceleration assumption.

The evidence supports improvement in the original operating concerns: US comps and Chinese growth are stronger than at entry. It does not itself identify the correct valuation. A current owner must ask how much of that recovery has become reflected in price, what growth remains and whether the expected return still exceeds the hurdle. No later China closures, revised guidance or pandemic losses inform that assessment.
docs.D04_price_valuation.md:
Title: January price versus entry valuation and the company's outlook
Source: compiled from: https://fiscal.ai/company/NASDAQ_SBUX/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/829224/000082922419000047/sbux-9292019xexhibit991.htm; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/10/07150943/2018-Annual-Report-Letter-Only.pdf
Date: 2020-01-15

Historical daily data show Starbucks opening at $91.00 and closing at $91.54 on January 15, on volume of 6,145,518 shares. Only that historical row is used from the modern price database; its current company description and later prices are excluded.

At $91.54, the stock trades at 32.3x FY2019 non-GAAP EPS of $2.83 and 31.3x GAAP EPS of $2.92. Using the FY2020 adjusted guidance midpoint of $3.025 gives 30.3x.

The original owner letter said the purchase came at a 25% discount to a historical average of 26x forward earnings, implying roughly 19.5x on the manager's then-forward denominator. That was an entry-period judgment, not a constant intrinsic-value formula.

The present 30.3x company-guidance multiple and the historical 26x reference use different dates and potentially different forward conventions. Nonetheless, the source evidence clearly no longer describes the same discounted entry setup.

The $91.54 close is 78.4% above the manager's stated $51.30 average entry price before dividends. This is a simple price comparison, not the fund's realized return, trading result or a claim that every share was sold on the cutoff.

Using FY2019 ending shares of 1,184.6 million gives an indicative equity value of $108.435 billion. Adding long-term debt less cash of $8.480 billion gives approximately $116.916 billion before lease/other enterprise adjustments and any post-year-end share changes.

The same equity proxy against FY2019 CFO-minus-capex of $3.240 billion gives approximately a 3.0% cash-flow yield. This is a backward-looking calculation, not a normalized forecast; FY2018's transaction-heavy cash flow would be particularly misleading.

A verified current 52-week range, daily five-year valuation series, forward peer multiples and S&P multiple were not recovered. No cheap/expensive percentile is invented.

The valuation tension is explicit: a strong franchise with improving operations can still have less prospective return after substantial appreciation. An owner can recognize continuing business quality while independently reassessing the price, the EPS-growth outlook and the opportunity cost of committed capital.
docs.D05_market_concerns.md:
Title: Current debate — recovery evidence versus growth and China risks
Source: compiled from: https://www.cnbc.com/2019/10/30/starbucks-sbux-earnings-q4-2019.html; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/829224/000082922419000047/sbux-9292019xexhibit991.htm
Date: 2019-10-30

CNBC's October 30 report says Starbucks beat quarterly revenue estimates and shares rose in extended trading. It notes US cafés grew traffic across all dayparts for the second consecutive quarter. That is a more constructive operating backdrop than the weak comparable-sales period described at entry.

The report nevertheless identifies real China concerns: growing competition from Luckin Coffee and the possibility of an economic slowdown. Starbucks' 5% China comparable-sales growth is evidence of current resilience, not a proof that those competitive risks are irrelevant.

A premium coffee franchise depends on repeated discretionary purchases. Its brand and convenience can support pricing power, but consumers retain alternatives ranging from lower-priced chains to independent cafés and at-home preparation.

Growth through a dense store network also creates execution challenges. New stores may cannibalize existing ones, digital orders can strain throughput and product complexity can increase labor demands. An attractive habit-based business still needs operational consistency.

The FY2020 adjusted EPS guidance range of $3.00-$3.05 represents roughly 6%-8% growth from FY2019's $2.83. At a premium earnings multiple, the market may be discounting either acceleration, durable long-term growth or both. A modest guidance miss could therefore matter even without permanent moat damage.

Buybacks deserve separate scrutiny. FY2019 repurchases exceeded $10 billion, compared with CFO-minus-capex of approximately $3.2 billion. Financing and prior transaction proceeds support the program, but continuing at the same pace indefinitely would require additional resources.

The balance sheet's $11.167 billion long-term debt and $2.687 billion cash also matter when assessing capital return. Per-share EPS improvement from fewer shares is not identical to growth in total earning power.

No major China closure announcement or later coronavirus operating shock is included. The information boundary is January 15, before the January 28 results and closure disclosures. Treating the January investment decision as an established pandemic-risk response would import unavailable evidence.

The contemporaneous debate is therefore valuation-sensitive, not a simple broken-business narrative: operating recovery is visible, China remains both a growth runway and a risk, and the price must justify the remaining cash-flow growth.
docs.D06_thesis_changes.md:
Title: What has changed since the original owner thesis
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/10/07150943/2018-Annual-Report-Letter-Only.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/829224/000082922419000047/sbux-9292019xexhibit991.htm; https://fiscal.ai/company/NASDAQ_SBUX/
Date: 2020-01-15

The original thesis combined a durable franchise, fixable operating disappointment, high-return expansion and a discounted valuation. These elements should be reassessed separately rather than treating the stock's appreciation as either automatic success or automatic overvaluation.

**US operations:** The owner letter described a period of only 1%-2% same-store growth, then early improvement to 4%. Q4 FY2019 US comparable sales grew 6%, with contemporary press reporting traffic growth across all dayparts. The operating repair has progressed in the available data.

**China:** The original growth runway remains supported by reported expansion: Q4 China comps grew 5% and net store count 17% year over year. Competition and macro risk persist. A continuing runway does not mean every future unit earns the manager's historical estimated pretax return.

**Digital/loyalty:** US active rewards membership reached 17.6 million, up 15%. That supports execution on one of the original initiatives. It does not independently quantify future incremental profit or remove normal customer-acquisition and reward costs.

**Capital allocation:** FY2019 repurchases exceeded $10 billion and diluted weighted-average shares declined materially. That validates substantial delivery of capital return, while also changing debt, cash and the future EPS denominator.

**Valuation:** The manager's entry argument was an approximately 25% discount to a 26x historical forward multiple. The January $91.54 close implies about 30.3x the company's FY2020 adjusted EPS midpoint. The original valuation gap has plainly changed, even allowing for differences in forward conventions.

**Forward growth:** FY2020 revenue guidance is 6%-8% and operating-income guidance 8%-10%, while adjusted EPS guidance implies roughly 6%-8%. The analyst must decide whether a higher long-term growth assumption is warranted, rather than carry forward past buyback-enhanced growth mechanically.

There is no dated evidence here that the core coffee moat has disappeared or that management is fundamentally untrustworthy. The changed facts mainly concern execution, price and capital structure.

That creates a genuine ownership decision: retain a high-quality compounding business at its current expected return, or release capital if the return no longer clears the hurdle. The pack supplies the comparison, not the manager's eventual answer.
docs.D07_pershing_context.md:
Title: Portfolio opportunity cost and restaurant concentration
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2019/08/20165951/PSH-2019-Interim-Financial-Statements1.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/10/07150943/2018-Annual-Report-Letter-Only.pdf
Date: 2019-08-15

The 2019 interim letter discusses a concentrated portfolio including Chipotle, Restaurant Brands, Hilton, Lowe's, ADP, Berkshire and the mortgage enterprises, as well as Starbucks. The names span different business models but include significant consumer/restaurant exposure.

The original annual letter reports PSH invested $495 million in Starbucks at an average $51.30. That is the listed vehicle's historical investment, not the all-funds approximately $900 million stake reported at initial disclosure.

The investor praised new-store returns, growth runway and the pricing opportunity. By the interim period, Starbucks was a substantial positive contributor to performance. Performance contribution, however, is not current position weight and should not be used to calculate precise remaining capacity.

The manager's Berkshire discussion in the same interim report provides an alternative style of exposure: a diversified insurer/industrial business with a large cash reserve and management succession in progress. That illustrates opportunity cost within an actual portfolio rather than an abstract comparison with the S&P.

Chipotle offers a more active restaurant-repair thesis; Restaurant Brands has franchise-fee economics. Starbucks combines owned stores, licensed operations and consumer habit. Similar industry labels do not imply identical margins, capex needs or risk, yet common consumer and valuation factors can affect them together.

Precise current manager-wide AUM, vehicle cash, January weights and transaction dates were not recovered from a qualifying pre-cutoff source. No post-cutoff monthly report revealing a sale is used.

An existing owner has different choices from a new buyer: maintaining, trimming, reallocating or fully exiting. Taxes, position liquidity, prospective return and the availability of new opportunities can all matter. The documented cost basis is relevant context, not a reason to anchor intrinsic value to past gains.

No evidence in this pack establishes a planned replacement security or requires an immediate sale simply because Starbucks appreciated. The business and valuation need to be evaluated against the portfolio's hurdle independently.

The portfolio context therefore helps separate three possible interpretations: core thesis impairment, fair-value realization and superior opportunity cost. It does not disclose which interpretation the manager ultimately adopted in January.

drivers.driver: Share-price appreciation compressed prospective returns as the investment approached estimated value.
The operating recovery and brand thesis worked; the exit did not require a conclusion that Starbucks was a broken business.
Release capital after attractive realized returns rather than retain the same valuation discount assumption indefinitely.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Eight documents including D00 and explicit thesis-change comparison. January15 $91.54/volume recovered; company full financials and forward guide used. Precise sale timing, current fund weights/AUM and full peer multiples missing. No January28 China closures or future pandemic evidence.

thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: US operations: strengthened, evidenced by traffic growth and sustained same-store sales recovery [D06, D07]
China growth: intact, with continued store expansion and comparable sales growth [D04, D07]
Operating initiatives: intact, with rewards membership growth and successful overhead simplification [D04, D07]
Valuation: broken (in terms of entry thesis), as the stock has appreciated significantly and now trades at a high multiple [D05, D07]
final.valuation_now: 30.3x FY2020 adjusted EPS guidance, a significant rerating from the original purchase [D05, D07]

drivers.driver: The stock has experienced significant appreciation, causing the forward IRR to fall below our 15% threshold for new or maintained high-conviction positions [D05, D07].

final.memo:
Our investment in the Company was predicated on a high-quality, habit-based business with significant runway for growth, which we were able to acquire at an attractive 25% discount to historical valuation [D00, D07]. Since our entry, the management team has successfully executed on our thesis, driving improved US traffic, increasing rewards membership, and expanding the franchise in China [D04, D06, D07]. These operational improvements are clear, and the core moat remains robust [D07].

However, the investment landscape has shifted significantly. The stock has appreciated roughly 78% since our average entry price [D05]. It now trades at approximately 30.3x our estimate of FY2020 adjusted earnings, a valuation that no longer offers the asymmetric upside we seek [D05, D07]. While the business remains a high-quality compounder, the current price largely reflects the successful execution of the operating turnaround, reducing the prospective forward return [D05, D07].

As stewards of our partners' capital, we must be disciplined in our hurdle rates. Given the substantial appreciation, the forward IRR no longer meets our 15% target for maintaining a concentrated position [D07]. We are trimming our holding to reallocate capital toward opportunities that offer more compelling risk-adjusted returns, while retaining a position in what remains an excellent franchise [D05, D07].
uncited_claims: The decision to trim is based on the discipline of harvesting gains when a valuation gap closes, even when the underlying business fundamentals remain strong.

drivers.driver: The stock's significant appreciation to a ~30x forward multiple has compressed prospective returns below our 15% hurdle [D05, D07].

final.memo:
Starbucks has been a successful investment, with the company delivering on the operational turnaround we anticipated [D04, D07]. US same-store sales growth has recovered to 6% in Q4, and the company continues to execute on its digital and loyalty initiatives, validating our original thesis regarding the franchise's durability and fixable operational path [D04, D07]. The growth runway in China remains significant, notwithstanding the competitive and macro risks [D04, D06, D07].

However, the valuation has shifted substantially since our initial investment at an average price of $51.30 [D05]. With the shares trading at $91.54, or approximately 30.3x FY2020 adjusted earnings guidance, the margin of safety provided by the entry discount has been entirely realized [D05, D07]. Given current growth guidance of 6-8% in adjusted EPS, the forward rate of return is no longer consistent with our 15% threshold for new or maintained high-conviction positions [D04, D07].

While the business remains a high-quality, free-cash-flow-generative compounder, we must be disciplined regarding opportunity cost [D07]. We are trimming the position to harvest gains as the stock price has outpaced the near-term growth in intrinsic value, and we believe our capital can be more effectively deployed in opportunities offering higher prospective returns [D05, D07].
